claims.text: The two groups show identical event patterns — each consists of six consecutive authentication‑failure lines from the same sshd process, all targeting the root account and reporting a “tty=NODEVssh” pseudo‑terminal.

In the first group (220.117.241.87) the failures occur within a 5‑second window starting at **19:15:48**, while in the second group (h64-187-1-131.gtconnect.net) they are spaced about two seconds apart, beginning at **12:11:53**.

Both sources repeatedly attempt to log in as root from a single remote host, but the first source’s attempts cluster tightly around a single minute (four distinct timestamps within 4 seconds), whereas the second source spreads them over roughly eight seconds with two events sharing the same second.

Because the first group’s bursts are more densely packed and occur at an unusual hour (19:15) compared with the broader, midday window of the second group, the former appears more anomalous in terms of timing concentration.

My root‑cause hypothesis is that the 220.117.241.87 source is likely part of a scripted brute‑force or credential‑stuffing campaign that rapidly re‑issues failed login attempts to exhaust the authentication queue, whereas the longer‑spaced attempts from h64-187-1-131.gtconnect.net may stem from a less aggressive, perhaps manually triggered, attack.
